## Design

### 2026-10-29: During the first hour and a half, I worked strictly on the design and component placement, searching the entire internet for the specific dimensions that would be suitable for my project. This took a

**4h**

During the first hour and a half, I worked strictly on the design and component placement, searching the entire internet for the specific dimensions that would be suitable for my project. This took a long time, especially since working with just a sheet of paper and a pencil was not very helpful.

I spent the next two and a half hours working in KiCad to create the electrical schematic. I also watched some tutorials online. It wasn't particularly difficult, but it was very tedious, as the library did not contain the specific symbols I needed. At one point, I realized that the symbols in KiCad were not matching the ones I was using

![1000013731](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ksX9hopTccFlCIaHXzVm1PZCSGSdh7qw/cfbb90334f999012d3e4038a580b0796282bbef778458c7bfd158c502d33c22e.jpg)

 which is why , I had to use single-row connectors (J1, J2, etc.) instead of the actual components. I named each connector after the corresponding component and labelled its pins accordingly, which allowed me to recreate the components without wasting valuable time creating the symbols myself.

Finally, I worked on connecting the components, which required a great deal of attention to detail.

### 2026-10-31: ![1000013810](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ksX9hopTccFlCIaHXzVm1PZCSGSdh7qw/92346f162695c21a9b61eb1c712b4a6094b76627a7b2aacf266434285729e2d8.jpg)

**4h**

![1000013810](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ksX9hopTccFlCIaHXzVm1PZCSGSdh7qw/92346f162695c21a9b61eb1c712b4a6094b76627a7b2aacf266434285729e2d8.jpg)

During this session, I created the ESP32 CH340 symbol in KiCad. It was quite a long process because I had to manually enter each pin, assign its Electrical Type, and arrange it using the correct X and Y coordinates.

I would say that the first step, entering the pins and assigning their electrical types, was the easiest part. After that, I accidentally used the pin layout from a different ESP32 board and ended up scattering the pins everywhere.

Once I found the correct pin layout for the ESP32 CH340 board, I had to realign all the pins from scratch, changing their X and Y coordinates wherever necessary. AND THAT TOOK FOREVERRR!

But in the end, I managed to create the symbol, and now I hope that if anyone ever needs it, they will be able to use mine!

During this session, I replaced every connector, whether it had 6, 8, or 30 pins, with the actual component symbol to make things easier for anyone who might want to recreate this project. Also, from the point where I left off, it should be relatively easy to add a footprint to each component and turn everything into a PCB, without having to use wires anymore.
Personally, I will connect everything using wires.
The reason it took me so long to work on just four components was not adding them to KiCad, but assigning the correct electrical type to each pin. I spent quite a while working on the PCM5102A because I researched the electrical types of the FLT, DEMP, XSMT, FMT, A3V3, AGND, ROUT, and LROUT pins, even though I later realized that I didn't actually need them when I looked at the electrical schematic.

![IMG_20261031_200642132_HDR](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/ksX9hopTccFlCIaHXzVm1PZCSGSdh7qw/ed50b32cbeb0f3b52d24966d3212077873920048f0132c7b6fd01720a378e0be.jpg)

The second component that took me a long time to figure out was the Memory Card Shield Module, as I also struggled to find the correct electrical types for its pins.
I think the main reason for this is simply that I don't really know how to search for this information properly yet. However, there's not much I can do about it. I'm still a beginner, and I'm learning as I go.
I had finished adding all the symbols and deleted Conn_01x30. I then added the ESP32 symbol and pressed Ctrl + S to save my work. A moment later, I suddenly realized that I shouldn't have deleted the connector because all my connections were attached to it. So, I had to search for the schematic online again and carefully reconnect every single wire. And once again, IT TOOK FOREVER!
